item.title: Raiders RB Dylan Laube named the AFC special teams player of the week
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: There were no kickoff returns for touchdowns in the first seven weeks of the 2026 season, but that streak came to an end in the second quarter of the Week 8 game between the Raiders and Jets at MetLife Stadium.
item.content:encoded:
There were no kickoff returns for touchdowns in the first seven weeks of the 2026 season, but that streak came to an end in the second quarter of the Week 8 game between the Raiders and Jets at MetLife Stadium.

After the Jets scored a touchdown to take a 13-7 lead, Raiders running back Dylan Laube fielded the ensuing kickoff and took it all the way to the end zone. Laube's 95-yard return gave the Raiders a lead that they'd fumble before recovering in the second half to earn a 38-33 win.

Laube added 49 yards on two other returns later in the game and he was named the AFC special teams player of the week on Wednesday.

Laube is the league leader with an average of 34.1 yards per kickoff return heading into Week 9. He'll try to hold onto that lead while facing the 49ers this Sunday.

(Photo by Rich Graessle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

After a four game losing streak, Kirk Cousins and Brock Bowers led the Las Vegas Raiders to a win over the New York Jets to stay in the playoff hunt. Mike Florio also wonders what comes next for Aaron Glenn's Jets.

item.title: Alex Anzalone earns first NFC defensive player of the week award
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: The Buccaneers beat the Falcons without completing a pass on Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
The Buccaneers beat the Falcons without completing a pass on Sunday.

They also beat the Falcons without allowing a point.

Linebacker Alex Anzalone was in the middle of that, and now he's been named NFC defensive player of the week.

Anzalone had two interceptions plus six tackles, including one for loss, in the Bucs’ 16-0 victory.

Both of his picks came in the first quarter. According to the league, he is just the second linebacker since 2000 to have two interceptions in the first quarter of a game. Lofa Tatupu also accomplished the feat in 2007.

This is Anzalone’s first career defensive player of the week award.

The Buccaneers will be on the road to face the Bears on Sunday night this week.

item.title: Jaguars S Rayuan Lane is the AFC defensive player of the week
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Jaguars had to turn to backup safeties due to injuries in last Sunday's game against the Colts and one of them came up with a huge play at the end of the first half.
item.content:encoded:
The Jaguars had to turn to backup safeties due to injuries in last Sunday's game against the Colts and one of them came up with a huge play at the end of the first half.

Rayuan Lane snagged a Daniel Jones pass that tight end Tyler Warren couldn't control and returned it 92 yards for a touchdown that pushed Jacksonville's lead to 28-0 before halftime. The Jaguars went on to win 42-7.

Lane ended the day with four tackles, three passes defensed and a quarterback hit. That effort led to him being named the AFC defensive player of the week on Wednesday.

Lane was a 2025 sixth-round pick and his play last Sunday could help him earn a continued role in the secondary with Eric Murray out for the season due to an elbow injury.

item.title: Tyler Allgeier wins first NFC offensive player of the week award
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: The Cardinals had injury concerns at running back during Sunday's comeback victory over the Cowboys.
item.content:encoded:
The Cardinals had injury concerns at running back during Sunday's comeback victory over the Cowboys.

But the player who stayed healthy was a big part of the win.

Now Tyler Allgeier has been named NFC offensive player of the week.

Allgeier had 191 yards from scrimmage including 147 yards rushing with two total touchdowns in the 33-30 victory. Both his yards from scrimmage and rushing yards were career-highs.

For Week 8, Allgeier led the league in scrimmage yards and was one of just three NFC players to record multiple scrimmage touchdowns.

This is Allgeier’s first offensive player of the week award. It’s the first time a Cardinals running back has earned the honor since Adrian Peterson in Week 6 of the 2017 season.

item.title: Tee Higgins named the AFC offensive player of the week
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: A pair of Bengals wide receivers had big games in Week 8, but only one of them could be named the AFC offensive player of the week.
item.content:encoded:
A pair of Bengals wide receivers had big games in Week 8, but only one of them could be named the AFC offensive player of the week.

The NFL announced that Tee Higgins was their choice for that award on Wednesday. Higgins had 10 catches for 155 yards and two touchdowns, which gave him the edge over Ja'Marr Chase. Chase finished the 43-36 overtime win with 11 catches for 141 yards and a touchdown.

Higgins's first score gave the Bengals a 21-13 lead in the third quarter and his second tied the game with 1:17 left to play in regulation.

It is the first time in his career that Higgins has taken weekly honors in the conference.

item.title: KC Concepcion: Browns are confident, getting Shedeur Sanders ready for Sunday
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The Browns haven't officially named Shedeur Sanders this week's starter, but with Deshaun Watson in the concussion protocol, all signs are pointing in that direction.
item.content:encoded:
The Browns haven't officially named Shedeur Sanders this week's starter, but with Deshaun Watson in the concussion protocol, all signs are pointing in that direction.

Those signs include Browns wide receiver KC Concepcion saying today that the offense is rallying around Sanders to get him ready to play against the Saints.

"It was unfortunate what happened to Deshaun, but we're going to pick up Shedeur's confidence, and get him ready for Sunday," Concepcion said.

Sanders lost a quarterback competition with Watson during the preseason, and Watson has played better than expected during the regular season. So Sanders has barely played this year, getting on the field just long enough to throw three passes. But on Sunday, he may start.

Last year Sanders started seven games as a rookie and struggled, but this year he'll get to show what kind of progress he's made. The Browns, who have playoff aspirations, have to hope he's ready.

item.title: Bryce Young, C.J. Stroud continue fourth seasons without new contracts
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: In theory, new deals could be done at any time.
item.content:encoded:
Several players taken in the first round of the 2023 NFL draft have gotten their second contracts. The first two players picked that year still have not.

Halfway through their fourth seasons, Panthers quarterback Bryce Young and Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud continue to play under their rookie deals.

As to Stroud, a subpar third season complicated negotiations. A decision was made to proceed with his fourth season, without a second deal.

A Tuesday article from ESPN took a close look at the respective preseason positions of player and team. The key facts: (1) the Texans offered a contract with a new-money value in excess of $50 million; and (2) Stroud did not ask to be the highest-paid quarterback in the league. (Patrick Mahomes currently leads the way at $63.093 million.)

Although the Texans have slumped to 2-5 in 2026, Stroud's play has improved significantly. A new deal — closer to the top of the market — becomes likely after the current season. It remains theoretically possible that the two sides could work something out sooner than that.

For the player, there's always an urgency to shift the injury risk to the team. Especially when the player will be assuming 60 minutes of injury risk, 17 times over.

As to Young, we've recently caught wind of chatter that the Panthers are "far down the road" toward signing him to a second deal in excess of $50 million per year.

Both are under contract through 2027, with their fifth-year options already exercised. For both, the guaranteed salary in 2027 will be $25.904 million. The franchise tag becomes an option for 2028, absent new deals.

Most teams prefer to make a final decision before then. Up or out. New contract, or find a new quarterback.

Again, both Young and Stroud are eligible for new contracts at any time. Both teams seem to want to keep them around. The only questions at this are when the deals will be one, what the new-money value will be, and (most importantly) how the payments will be structured — especially as to guarantees.

item.title: Report: Jordyn Tyson will return to practice on Wednesday
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: There is some positive news on the injury front for the Saints as they return from their bye week.
item.content:encoded:
There is some positive news on the injury front for the Saints as they return from their bye week.

Rookie receiver Jordyn Tyson is set to return to practice on Wednesday, according to Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.football.

Tyson has been sidelined by a hamstring injury since training camp. He was placed on injured reserve with a designation to return when rosters were reduced to 53 players.

The Saints will have 21 days to activate Tyson to the 53-man roster.

The No. 8 overall pick of this year’s draft, Tyson should provide a boost to a team that is No. 14 in points scored and No. 23 in total yards.

The Saints will return to action at home against the Browns on Sunday.

item.dc:creator: Josh Alper

item.content:encoded:
The Falcons held a walkthrough upon arriving in Madrid on Wednesday and they release their estimated practice report for the day after that session came to an end.

Linebacker James Pearce took part in the walkthrough and was listed as a full participant as he moves toward making his 2026 debut. Pearce missed the first eight games while serving a Personal Conduct Policy suspension related to a domestic violence incident earlier this year.

Wide receiver Zachariah Branch (hamstring) was the only player listed as out of practice. The Falcons announced earlier this week that Branch will not play against the Bengals on Sunday. Defensive end Samson Ebukam was also ruled out before being placed on injured reserve on Tuesday.

Linebacker Yasir Abdullah (hamstring), linebacker Divine Deablo (forearm), and running back Brian Robinson (hamstring) were listed as limited participants. Defensive back Billy Bowman (hamstring), wide receiver Beaux Collins (hip), and offensive tackle Cameron Williams (ankle) were listed as full participants.

item.title: Nebraska voters say no to mobile sports betting
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: If you haven't heard, Tuesday was election day.
item.content:encoded:
If you haven't heard, Tuesday was election day. Multiple candidates with NFL connections lost.

In Nebraska, the sports books also lost.

Via Erin Bamer of the Nebraska Examiner, voters there rejected online sports betting.

The ballot initiative came after multiple efforts by gambling interests to legalize it through the legislative process, which has been successful in many other states.

The outcome in Nebraska raises an obvious question. How many states in which their elected representatives embraced sports betting would have rejected it, if the people had the right to vote on it?

For those charged with balancing the public budget, tax revenues from legalized sports betting become a siren's song. And it results in plenty of citizens wrecking their own finances by chasing the false promise of easy money.

Earlier this year, Warren Buffett called sports betting a "tax on stupidity." All gambling is, really. The system is designed to take your money, either quickly or slowly. Any wins will be outweighed over time by the losses.

If that wasn't the case, the sports books wouldn't be in business. And the states wouldn't embrace the easy money that comes from aligning with the house and indirectly increasing the taxes of those who choose to participate.

Because the house always wins. Except in states where the people are given the chance to vote on whether the vampire will be invited onto their phones.

item.title: 2026 season could highlight the unfairness of the eight-division structure
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: It's time to consider ditching the two-conference, eight-division approach.
item.content:encoded:
From time to time, the NFL's current structure has created unfair results, with the best of four bad teams assigned to a predetermined division earning a playoff berth and the home game that goes along with it.

This year, the NFC has two very strong divisions, one so-so division, and one very weak division.

Here's the basic reality. With the four NFC division winners getting tickets to the playoff party, the wild-card berths will go to three teams. And, currently, there are three teams in the NFC North and two in the NFC West that are potentially better than whoever will win the NFC East and the NFC South.

Between the Vikings, Bears, Lions, Packers, 49ers, Seahawks, and Rams, two will be crowned division winners. That leaves five for the wild-card berths.

Ultimately, two of them will be frozen out of the playoffs — even if both of those teams end up with better records than the best teams of the NFC East and NFC South.

During last Friday's episode of PFT Live, I threw out an alternative approach that would be far more fair to all teams.

Instead of two conferences with a quartet of four-team divisions, why not pivot to four eight-team divisions?

NFL East, NFL North, NFL South, NFL West. The easiest configuration would consist of slapping the current East, North, South, and West divisions into one conference each. While some tweaks could be needed to better align things geographically, it would be far more fair to guarantee a playoff spot (and a home game) to the best of eight teams, not the best of four teams.

Decisions would have to be made about scheduling. The home-and-home series (a vestige of the days when there were far fewer teams) would need to be retired. Each team would play the seven other teams in its conference, with 10 (or 11, inevitably) other games.

The playoffs would consist of the four conference champions (with the best two getting byes) and 10 wild-card teams. And there would be an added benefit — it would be possble to have the best two teams meet in the Super Bowl, without regard to the traditional AFL-NFL/AFC-NFC separation.

It would be one league. One playoff tree. Any combination of teams would, in theory, be possible for the Super Bowl. When the dust settles on the semifinal round, the best two teams would remain.

That said, it won't be easy to get the owners to give up the current format, which entails in any given year a one-in-four shot at hosting a playoff game. But if the goal is to constantly strive for ways to create more compelling matchups, an eight-team, four-conference approach makes a lot more sense than the current structure.

Football is a meritocracy. A configuration of four, eight-team conferences would be far more conducive to that ideal.

Will it happen? Probably not. Should it be taken seriously by the league? Absolutely.

Maybe this year, when the NFC East and NFC South provide none-of-the-above champions and two very viable teams are sent home after Week 18, will spark a real conversation about meaningful change.

item.title: Report: Tyler Huntley to miss the rest of 2026 season
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Huntley injured his toe in last Sunday's loss to the Bills.
item.content:encoded:
Ravens quarterback Tyler Huntley's season is reportedly over.

Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that tests on Huntley's toe showed a turf toe injury that will require him to miss the rest of the team's games.

Huntley had already been ruled out for Thursday night's game against the Jaguars, which has undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano in line to make his first NFL start. With Lamar Jackson dealing with a thumb injury that could also keep him out for the season, Fagnano could have an extended run in the starting job unless the Ravens opt to move in a different direction.

Kedon Slovis and Austin Reed are the other in-house options, but both of them just signed with the team this week so it's less than an ideal situation for the Ravens' bid to stay in the AFC playoff race.

item.title: Browns announce Deshaun Watson is in concussion protocol
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Watson developed symptoms on Monday night, after first-quarter helmet-to-helmet hit.
item.content:encoded:
Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders may be getting more than a handful of snaps in Week 9, when his team visits the Saints.

The Browns have announced that starting quarterback Deshaun Watson is in the concussion protocol.

"During the first quarter of Sunday's game against the Steelers, Deshaun took a helmet-to-helmet hit," the team said in a statement released on Wednesday morning. "The ATC spotter called down to the sideline, and the Unaffiliated Neurotrauma Consultant (UNC) administered a gameday concussion evaluation. Deshaun was cleared by the UNC and returned on the Browns' next offensive series. As part of the protocol, the team's medical staff evaluated him again postgame and Monday morning. Both times he showed no symptoms, passed his evaluations, and was cleared. On Tuesday morning, he reported to the medical staff that he began experiencing concussion symptoms Monday night and was immediately placed in the concussion protocol."

Watson will remain in the concussion protocol until he clears the various steps. Until then, Sanders will presumably be the starter — unless the coaching staff decides to pivot to Dillon Gabriel.

The development comes not long after Sanders hired an agent for the first time, presumably in an effort to secure a trade to a new team. For now, he'll get a chance to make the case to become the eventual starter for the Browns. Or to attract interest elsewhere in him once 2027 rolls around.

For the 5-3 Browns, it's a significant development. They need to keep pace with the 6-2 Steelers and 5-2 Bengals. Picking up a fourth loss without Watson (who eventually threw for 324 yards in the 27-6 loss at Pittsburgh) will make that harder to accomplish.

item.title: Bills reverse course on "high-maintenance" C.J. Gardner-Johnson
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The Bills said they'd be keeping safety C.J.
item.content:encoded:
The Bills said they'd be keeping safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson. And now they're not.

Tuesday's surprise move to release the veteran defensive back directly contradicts the comments made publicly by coach Joe Brady, on the same day Gardner-Johnson received a one-game suspension for spitting on an opponent during the Week 6 game against the Raiders.

“Look, C.J.'s a member of the Buffalo Bills,” Brady said on October 19. “We brought him here for a reason, and we know that he knows that he has to play better. He knows he has to be better for this team, and, you know, just like everybody else, right, we’ve got to learn from this stuff, and we have to improve and find ways to get better as the season goes.”

And now Gardner-Johnson is gone.

As one source explained it to PFT, the Bills decided that Gardner-Johnson was simply too "high-maintenance" — and that the talent and production didn't justify the headaches.

Plenty of other teams could have told the Bills what would happen. Gardner-Johnson has hopscotched around the league, from the Saints to the Eagles to the Lions to the Eagles (again) to the Texans to the Ravens to the Bears to the Bills.

He has been good enough to get more chances, but not good enough to keep him around in light of the issues that he brings with him.

The Bills hoped to harness his attitude in order to give the defense a lift. In the end, however, the baggage outweighed the boost.

And now Gardner-Johnson becomes a free agent again. Plenty of coaches believe they can be the one to speak to a player's better angels. As to Gardner-Johnson, the demons have won, far too often.

item.title: Most Cowboys players left facility on Monday before locker-room media availability
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The day after an embarrassing home loss to the Cardinals — who have never lost at AT&T Stadium — many of the Cowboys' players skipped a session with the media covering the team.
item.content:encoded:
The day after an embarrassing home loss to the Cardinals — who have never lost at AT&T Stadium — many of the Cowboys' players skipped a session with the media covering the team.

"The Cowboys just had locker room availability, but majority of roster left the facility before we got in there," Jon Machota of The Athletic said. "No players were interviewed. Can’t say I remember that happening before."

There's an explanation, as there often is. Via Joseph Hoyt of the Dallas Morning News, the "player programs ended earlier than scheduled, which is why the locker room was almost empty during media availability."

Making players available in the locker room is one of the basic weekly obligations for all teams. Whatever the reason, it's likely few were inclined to say anything about Sunday's game.

Especially since the Cowboys blew a 14-point lead at home for the first time in franchise history. Against a two-win team that has inexplicably owned the Cowboys in recent years.

item.title: Lions put LB Jimmy Rolder on IR, waive DB Bishop Fitzgerald
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Lions announced that linebacker Jimmy Rolder suffered a season-ending hamstring injury during Sunday's win over the Vikings and they moved him to the injured reserve list.
item.content:encoded:
The Lions announced that linebacker Jimmy Rolder suffered a season-ending hamstring injury during Sunday's win over the Vikings and they moved him to the injured reserve list.

Rolder was injured on the same play that linebacker Jack Campbell suffered a neck injury that has required him to remain hospitalized since Sunday. The fourth-round pick had 11 tackles and a sack in his five appearances during the regular season.

Lions head coach Dan Campbell said that the team will sign linebacker K.J. Britt off of the Patriots' practice squad.

They have another open roster spot at their disposal as well. They announced that defensive back Bishop Fitzgerald has been waived on Tuesday.

Fitzgerald was signed off of the Steelers' practice squad in September, but he never appeared in a game for the Lions.

item.title: Mike Macdonald wants Seahawks to "focus on recapturing us"
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: After Monday night's loss to the Bears, Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said that his team was beaten in all three phases of the game and he revisited that line of thinking on Tuesday.
item.content:encoded:
After Monday night's loss to the Bears, Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said that his team was beaten in all three phases of the game and he revisited that line of thinking on Tuesday.

During an appearance on Seattle Sports 710, Macdonald said that there's an "itch to say" what needs to change about the team as they work to move forward from both the loss and the 4-4 start to their Super Bowl title defense. Macdonald then pivoted to suggesting "a deep breath" and a recentering of the things that propelled the Seahawks to success in the past rather than reaching for things to tweak across the board.

"If we're going to go out, we want to go out in our way and our style, and that wasn't us, or the best version of us at least," Macdonald said, via the team's website. "So that's why I think it's so tough. We have to focus on recapturing us and making sure that we're us when we turn the tape on. There were too many times throughout that game where that wasn't us in terms of just our style of ball. That's where we need to get better."

A home game against the Cardinals will be this week's opportunity to double down on the kind of recentering that Macdonald is talking about and getting that in place in time for the Seahawks to finish strong appears to be the path Macdonald is charting in Seattle.

item.title: Josh Jacobs needs to display more (or any) contrition
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: In May 2026, Packers running back Josh Jacobs crossed a line that should never be crossed.
item.content:encoded:
In May 2026, Packers running back Josh Jacobs crossed a line that should never be crossed. And neither he nor his representatives are acting accordingly in what should be an effort to seek redemption.

He pleaded no contest to battery of a woman. He's fighting in court to keep the video secret. He's responding to additional allegations through a strident statement from his lawyers attacking the accusers.

The most tone-deaf gesture of all came last Thursday night, when he celebrated a touchdown by pretending to wear, and to be released from, handcuffs.

His implausible explanation, which accused Prime Video of not showing enough of the celebration and attacked the media for interpreting the images with their lyin' eyes, was contradicted by the full video of the event.

That's not the way to play this. His no-contest plea is equivalent to saying, "I did it." He should be contrite. He should be apologetic. He should be seeking redemption.

The Packers continue to stand behind him, primarily because he's the best running back on the roster and they want to win games. Their reported interest in Colts running back Jonathan Taylor strongly suggests that, if the Packers could get Taylor, the support for Jacobs would immediately evaporate.

Here's the basic reality. If the Packers were to cut Jacobs, would anyone sign him? The Chiefs took plenty of heat last week for adding kicker Justin Tucker to the practice squad; they may not be inclined to give another second chance to a player whose arrival would compound the negative reaction to Tucker's arrival.

The reality, in every sport at every level, is obvious. If the player has enough skill and ability, someone will find a way to justify behavior that shouldn't be tolerated by an industry that relies so heavily on support from the public, both directly through ticket sales and TV ratings and indirectly through taxpayer funding for stadium projects.

Still, Jacobs has done himself no favors by adopting a posture of defiance. He did something no man should ever do. He's lucky he's good enough at football to not lose his job over it.

If he was at the bottom of the depth chart in Green Bay, he would have been gone a long time ago.

item.title: Jerry Jones claims (incorrectly) that there's "no correlation" between coaching pay and winning
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Jerry prefers to hire a cheap, unproven coach — and to hope he strikes gold.
item.content:encoded:
Jerry Jones has said that the size of the check he would write to guarantee another Super Bowl win would be "embarrassing."

Yes, it would be embarrassingly small.

Jones, when it comes to the resources he is willing to invest in the team, is cheap. He won't fire coaches who have buyouts. And he won't pay top dollar for new coaches.

The owner and G.M. of the Cowboys defended his approach during his latest visit to 105.3 The Fan in Dallas by making the nonsensical claim that there's no connection between coaching pay and winning.

"In the NFL, this is after years of looking at all the teams and all the coaches, there is no — there is zero correlation between how much you pay a coach, or how many coaches you have, as to winning," Jones said. "There is no correlation. And that's a random sample of years and all 32 teams involved.  So put that in your hopper and smoke it."

He's just wrong. Hiring a proven coach, and paying him accordingly, can change everything. We've seen it, time and again.

Andy Reid instantly turned the Chiefs into consistent contenders, and three-time Super Bowl winners. Sean Payton has made the Broncos into an annual contender, positioning him to become the first coach to win a Super Bowl for two different teams. Most recently, John Harbaugh has immediately changed everything for the Giants.

Harbaugh's success will result in his former rival, Mike Tomlin, fending off teams willing to pay him upwards of $30 million per year to swap out his earpiece and microphone on the NBC sideline set for the Sony headset along the white stripe.

Jones prefers to speculate, when it comes to coaches. In lieu of paying for a coach who has proven that he can win, Jones wants to roll the dice on an unproven commodity in the hopes of maximizing the return on his investment.

"You can be pretty creative in hiring your coaches," Jones said. "You can be creative sometime when you don't even know you're hiring the coaches.  And so I've had some good experience of hiring people who have never been in the NFL. I've had some experience of hiring young coaches, older coaches, and so, of course, you constantly remind me, as you should, of what my record is. And I understand that.  But I also know that the next time you throw the pick, if you were the old California gold miner, you may hit the Comstock Lode. And then it is gloryhole."

"Creative" is another way of saying "cheap." Buy low, and reap the benefit when the less expensive option yields results. And stick with him until his contract expires, to avoid having to pay two coaches at the same time.

It would be different if there truly was no correlation between quality (and cost) of coach and winning. But there ABSOLUTELY is a connection.

Still, Jerry prefers to dig through the bargain bin in search of an abandoned Botticelli. His own twist on "if you have to ask you can't afford it" is "if you have to ask I don't want it."

It's no surprise. In the early days of the salary cap, members of the media often pointed out that there's no cap on coaching pay. In time, the NFL realized, "Oh shit, there's no cap on coaching pay."

That has led to what some believe is an effort to collectively keep coaching pay from growing at the rate that it should. And some in league circles are convinced that Jerry Jones is the ringleader of what is, as a practical matter, an effort to collude.

Even if he's not going to pay top-of-market money for a coach, the higher the market goes, the more expensive it gets across the board. The rising tide, in other words, raises all dinghies. And Jerry would much rather spend his money on his aircraft carrier that has been retrofitted into a luxury hotel.

That's his prerogative. But Cowboys fans — who fork over their money and who devote their time and attention to watching games on TV and consuming Cowboys content — should understand what's going on. Jerry Jones is pinching pennies when it comes to paying coaches. As a result, he's often getting what he isn't paying for.

His mindset is highly relevant to the looming wreckage of the 2026 season. If coach Brian Schottenheimer has guaranteed money left on his contract for 2027, he will not be fired. And if Jones can avoid owing Schottenheimer a buyout, Jones will resist joining the pursuit of Tomlin, who admitted on the most recent edition of Football Night in America that he grew up a fan of the Cowboys.

Actually, that could make Jerry think that deep-seated rooting interest will give him a chance at hiring Tomlin on the cheap. Because cheap does as cheap is. And, when it comes to his team (and specifically to his coaches), Jerry Jones is cheap.

item.title: Jerry Jones wants to see more targets for George Pickens
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The 3-5 Cowboys have plenty of problems.
item.content:encoded:
The 3-5 Cowboys have plenty of problems. During the first of his two weekly radio spots on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas, owner and G.M. Jerry Jones mentioned one specific thing that he'd like to see change.

Regarding receiver George Pickens, Jones said this, via Jon Machota of The Athletic: "He needs the ball coming his way more."

Through eight games, Pickens has 62 targets. In Week 8 against the Cardinals, Pickens had the ball thrown in his direction only four times. Against the Eagles in Week 7, Pickens had six targets.

He has 39 catches for 533 yards and two touchdowns in 2026. That projects to 83 catches for 1,132 yards and 8.5 touchdowns.

In 2025, Pickens finished with 93 receptions, 1,429 yards, and nine scores.

Hovering over the situation is the decision the Cowboys will have to make after the season. He's making $27.298 million under the franchise tag; they could tag him again next year, at $32.758 million. Which is still nearly $10 million behind the top of the receiver market.

There's another option, now that the Cowboys are fading in the race for the NFC East title. They could make Pickens available in trade.

Would a contender offer a second-round pick for him? The Chiefs are currently desperate for help at receiver; they're interested (we're told) in Jaguars receiver Brian Thomas Jr. and Colts receiver Josh Downs. If the Chiefs are in on Pickens, other teams in the AFC (like the Bills) should be thinking about it, too.

If the Cowboys were to decide to make a move, they could stockpile a pick or two — and save $15.17 million in cash and cap space. For now, who knows? The Cowboys seem to be deluding themselves into thinking they're still contenders.

Unless that's just part of the annual effort to keep their fans coughing up cash for tickets and merch. Which continues to work very well, relative to the on-field production.

For 31 years, and counting.

item.title: Peyton Manning, Greg Olsen emerge as the potential Troy Aikman replacement
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: As the clock continues to tick toward a potential, if not inevitable, breakup between ESPN and Troy Aikman, a replacement will be needed on Monday Night Football if/when Aikman leaves.
item.content:encoded:
As the clock continues to tick toward a potential, if not inevitable, breakup between ESPN and Troy Aikman, a replacement will be needed on Monday Night Football if/when Aikman leaves.

Greg Olsen's name previously had emerged as a clear favorite, and for good reason. He's done the job at the highest level, and he has won multiple Emmys for it.

But there's already a big name who is in the Disney tent, and who already works on most Monday nights: Peyton Manning.

Via Sam Neumann of Awful Announcing, Andrew Marchand of The Athletic recently characterized Olsen as the favorite in a Q&A column — but also planted a flag as to the Peyton possibility.

Beyond putting someone in the booth who would perhaps instantly become the best analyst of them all, the move would give both ESPN and Manning an exit ramp from the ManningCast, which no longer moves the needle for ESPN2.

The question becomes whether Manning wants to do it, and whether ESPN would compensate him at market level. With his long-time rival Tom Brady getting $37.5 million per year from Fox, Manning would want to be close to that.

Or maybe to surpass it.

That simple fact makes it far more likely that, when the dust settles, it'll be Olsen and not Manning as the Aikman replacement.

item.title: Bob Heinz, member of undefeated 1972 Dolphins' "No-Name Defense," dies at 79
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Bob Heinz, a member of the undefeated 1972 Miami Dolphins' "No-Name Defense" and winner of two Super Bowl rings, has died at the age of 79.
item.content:encoded:
Bob Heinz, a member of the undefeated 1972 Miami Dolphins' "No-Name Defense" and winner of two Super Bowl rings, has died at the age of 79.

Heinz was born and raised in Milwaukee but went out West to play his college football at the University of the Pacific. After an excellent college career, he was a second-round pick of the Dolphins in 1969.

The Dolphins defense that Heinz joined was known as the No-Name Defense, a term given to them by Cowboys coach Tom Landry, who called them "a bunch of no-names." Some players might have taken offense, but the members of the Dolphins' defense embraced it as a term that showed they were greater as a unit than any of them would have been individually.

Heinz was a starting defensive tackle on both the 1972 Dolphins team that remains the only undefeated, untied team in NFL history, and the 1973 Dolphins, who repeated as Super Bowl champions. He missed the entire 1975 season with an injury, but returned in 1976 and 1977. He finished his NFL career with one season in Washington in 1978.

item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk has taken a significant step toward getting back on the field.
item.content:encoded:
Wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk has taken a significant step toward getting back on the field.

Aiyuk's agent Drew Rosenhaus told Adam Schefter of ESPN that his client has filed for reinstatement from the 49ers' reserve/left squad list. Rosenhaus also said that Aiyuk plans on reporting to the 49ers' facility this week.

“Brandon is healthy and ready to get back on the field,” Rosenhaus said.

Aiyuk landed on the list due to a protracted standoff with the 49ers about how he chose to rehab his 2024 knee injury and that included the 49ers' decision to void the remaining guarantees in his contract. The 49ers said that Aiyuk will never play for the team again, which would leave them with the choices of trading or releasing him once Aiyuk's reinstatement is processed and he reports to the team. Previous attempts to trade him drew no success, so a release may be the likeliest outcome.

item.title: Todd Monken expects to see sacks start to "pile up" for Jared Verse
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Browns defensive end Jared Verse made a fair amount of noise heading into Sunday's game against the Steelers, but he was mostly silent on the field in Pittsburgh.
item.content:encoded:
Browns defensive end Jared Verse made a fair amount of noise heading into Sunday's game against the Steelers, but he was mostly silent on the field in Pittsburgh.

Verse had one tackle in the 27-6 Steelers win and that continued the slow start to his Browns tenure. Verse had 8.5 sacks and 34 quarterback hits in 20 total games for the Rams in 2025, but had no sacks and six quarterback hits since coming to Cleveland in the Myles Garrett trade.

At a Monday press conference, Browns head coach Todd Monken was asked about the lack of splash plays and whether the expectations for immediate impact were unrealistic. Monken preached patience while expressing confidence that bigger things are coming for Verse.

“Well, I think it’s too early to say anything. I mean, I love the way Jared works every day since he’s come here, just like all of our guys, he loves to work," Monken said, via a transcript from the team. "He likes being on the field and practicing. And I think it’s a matter of adapting to our style, which is, you know, there are some things that aren’t as similar to what he was used to doing with the Rams and the attack style. And I think it’s just a matter of time before, you know, he really gets comfortable in what we’re doing defensively. And it’s unfair to compare him to Myles Garrett. I think that’s always been unfair. Myles is in an elite category of his own. That’s okay. I mean, that’s who he is. But we just need Jared to be the best version of Jared, and I think we’re going to continue to see growth there. And again, what will help us? Be ahead in games, force the other team to throw it, and I think you’ll start to see his sacks start to pile up.”

The Browns have a 5-3 record despite the lack of contributions from Verse, but their hopes of making a playoff push over the second half would feel stronger if he starts making more headlines with his play than his locker room quotes.

item.title: Jaguars' defense aiming for 25th straight game not allowing a 75-yard rusher
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Down to their third-string quarterback, the Ravens will likely need a big game from Derrick Henry.
item.content:encoded:
With the Ravens down to their third-string quarterback on Thursday night against the Jaguars, Baltimore will rely heavily on running back Derrick Henry. Unfortunately for the Ravens, it's been a long time since a running back has had a big game against the Jaguars' defense.

The Jaguars haven't allowed an opposing runner to gain 75 or more yards in a game in the last 24 games. If the Jaguars don't allow a 75-yard runner against the Ravens on Thursday night, they will become just the third team in the Super Bowl era to go 25 straight games without allowing an opposing runner to gain 75 yards.

Henry is leading the NFL with 158 rushing attempts this season, and he may very well get the ball even more than 20 times per game he's averaging so far this season. Undrafted rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano is making the first start of his career for the Ravens, so they're likely to need to get a big game running the ball if they're going to pull off the upset over the Jaguars.

Although Henry is still carrying the ball a lot at the age of 32, his effectiveness has waned. He's averaging a career-low 4.0 yards per carry. It won't be easy to have a breakout game against the Jaguars, but the Ravens need him to do it.
